summary: Tenant cookie path collision from client-side override causes pinned-model affinity to drop and fallback routing
description: Issue summary: Several customers on dedicated accounts (first reported by Arcadia HealthTech) are observing intermittent loss of pinned-model affinity during weighted canary rollouts. When affinity drops the request is routed to a fallback variant which increases error rate and token cost for affected tenants. Impact: customer-facing sessions see mixed-model outputs and increased latency/cost. Customer reports impact on live inference for scheduled traffic windows. Environment: prod, us-west-2, dedicated GPU cluster. Observed behavior vs expected: observed affinity drops when tenant session cookie is present but path attribute differs between initial request and edge rehydration. Expected: session/tenant cookie should be preserved across edge and sidecar hop and not cause unpin. This appears correlated to a client-side SDK that writes a tenant cookie with a root path and the edge-side sidecar rewriting cookies without preserving the original path attribute, causing downstream host/path mismatches and the routing mesh to treat the session as new (losing model pin).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a tenant on dedicated capacity and pin to rw-7b-instruct-v2 via route configuration.
2) Use a client that sets a tenant cookie at path '/' while initial edge handshake uses '/api/v1' path on the gateway (Arcadia SDK behavior).
3) Send a steady stream of chat/infer requests while a weighted canary is active for the pin's route (10% weight).
4) Observe that after a subset of requests the session affinity token changes and requests are routed to fallback variant; the model pin is effectively lost for that session.
5) Reproduce by toggling the client cookie Path attribute or by introducing a path-normalizing header rewrite at the sidecar to simulate the condition.
logs: [2026-03-10T14:22:03Z] edge-proxy.INFO tenant=arcadia uid=abc123 cookie=(tenant=arcadia; Path=/) routed=pin(rw-7b-instruct-v2)
[2026-03-10T14:22:08Z] router.WARN session=abc123 affinity-mismatch detected: cookie-path-mismatch -> fallback-route selected=rw-legacy-6b
investigation_notes: Initial triage by support: verified customer traffic and captured request/response headers; confirmed cookie Path attribute differs between client and sidecar-set cookie.

Hypothesis A: sidecar cookie rewrite (pre-commit sanitizer) removes or normalizes Path to the upstream route, causing the edge lookup to miss the tenant cookie on subsequent incoming requests routed by path.
Hypothesis B: client SDK sets cookie with domain/path that is incompatible with edge host rewrite during canary mirror, resulting in two different cookie values and session split.
Correlated with recent sidecar release (sidecar v1.9.2) which added stricter cookie Path normalization: see PR github.com/redwood-inference/sidecar/pull/1198.
Reproduced internally by replaying capture with synthetic client that flips Path between '/' and '/api/v1' and saw router selecting fallback when header mismatch occurs.
Edge-proxy metrics show spike in routing decisions to fallback variant exactly when cookies differ; no GPU OOMs or autoscaler events observed during window.
comments: Support (Aisha): Thanks Arcadia for logs and HAR. We've isolated cookie path mismatch as likely cause. We've escalated to sidecar and routing owners. (2026-03-10)
SRE (Miguel): Assigned and reproducing locally. Creating a test harness to simulate path rewrite and cookie behavior. Will instrument router to emit full-cookie-match diagnostics. (2026-03-11)
Customer (Arcadia): We rolled back sidecar agent on our hosts to prior version; issue frequency reduced but not eliminated — still seeing occasional affinity drops. (2026-03-11)

Sidecar Eng (Priya Rao): Sidecar PR added Path-normalization to avoid duplicate cookies across route mounts; we didn't anticipate interaction with tenant pin lookup which matches exact cookie string. Looking into backward-compatible fix. (2026-03-12)

Support (Aisha): Temporary mitigation suggested: configure client SDK to set cookie Path explicitly to match gateway mount (/api/v1) or enable 'preserve_cookie_path' in route config for affected tenant. Asked for confirmation from engineering if 'preserve_cookie_path' is safe at scale. (2026-03-12)
resolution_summary: In progress. Short-term mitigation recommended (customer-side change to cookie Path or route config 'preserve_cookie_path') reduced incidents for Arcadia. Engineering to deliver a sidecar patch that will preserve original cookie Path or standardize pin lookup to be path-agnostic. PR planned to update router pinning lookup logic and sidecar sanitizer to include original Path in a dedicated header for robust matching. Follow-up steps: (1) sidecar fix (target hotfix v1.9.3), (2) router change to perform path-agnostic cookie match, (3) rollout canary for patch to 5% then 25% then 100% with monitoring. Expected next update 2026-03-15.
